habitat: Well-wooded rivers, large dams, pans, estuaries and mangrove lagoons. Usually single, hunting by day from a low branch, a dead tree or the shoreline, and less secretive than the bitterns.
summary: A small heron with grey-green upperparts, creamy feather edges, grey sides of the neck and flanks, and a black cap. The yellow feet are prominent on take-off. The immature is dark above with whitish spots on the folded wings. When flushed it gives a sharp kew.

similar.note: A young Little Bittern has tawny folded wings. A young Green-backed Heron has dark upperparts with whitish spots on the folded wings.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^11=2048 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 1024–4096.

calls.description: A sharp, startling kew when flushed. The texts do not separate the sexes. Grade A from South Africa, filed under the older name Butorides striata and labelled Green-backed Heron.
